_comment: Plain-English labels and one-line explanations for everything a PM sees on screen. SINGLE source of truth: the UI (interface/*) reads these through knowledge_engine/ui_labels.py, and the Agent's system prompt builds its TERMS glossary from the same entries, so screen and chat use the same words. `label` is what is shown; `term` is the market shorthand it stands for (shown only in the tooltip / on request); `tip` is the one-line explanation. Audience: quantitative PMs who are comfortable with sigma, vol, forwards and probability but new to FX-options structuring. Edit wording here — no Python change needed (restart to pick up edits; loader is cached).

forward.label: Forward
forward.tip: The market forward rate for your horizon: spot adjusted for the interest-rate difference between the two currencies.

implied_vol.label: Implied vol (ATM)
implied_vol.tip: At-the-money implied volatility for this horizon: the market's price for how much the pair is expected to move.

target_distance_fwd.label: Target distance from forward
target_distance_fwd.tip: How far your target is from the forward, in standard deviations of the move over the horizon (σ). The Put/Call tag is the option side your target implies.

target_distance_spot.label: Target distance from spot
target_distance_spot.tip: The same measure, from today's spot instead of the forward.

carry.label: Carry (in vols)
carry.tip: Forward drift over the horizon divided by the horizon's volatility: ln(forward ÷ spot) ÷ (σ√T). Positive means the forward is above spot.

carry_vs_vol.label: Carry vs vol
carry_vs_vol.tip: Whether carry is large enough relative to vol to matter. Low: carry is noise next to vol. Moderate or High: carry is a real factor in the trade.

carry_payout_ratio.label: Carry payout ratio
carry_payout_ratio.tip: Payout-to-cost ratio of the spread that captures carry (ATM-forward vs ATM-spot). Higher means carry capture is better rewarded. It does not say whether carry helps or hurts your view.

rate_base.label: {ccy} rate
rate_base.tip: Base-currency interest rate for the horizon, read from the discount curve.

rate_quote.label: {ccy} rate (implied)
rate_quote.tip: Quote-currency rate implied by the forward (covered interest parity).

skew.label: Skew
skew.tip: 25Δ call vol minus 25Δ put vol. Positive: base-currency calls are priced richer than puts, so the market pays up for upside in the base currency.

smile_curvature.label: Smile curvature
smile_curvature.tip: Average of the 25Δ call and put vols, minus ATM vol: how much the wings are priced above the middle.

stop_distance.label: Stop distance ({rr:.1f}:1 reward-to-risk)
stop_distance.tip: Move to target ÷ reward-to-risk: how far the forward can reverse before the stop level.

stop_level.label: Stop level
stop_level.tip: The forward level that corresponds to the stop distance.

loss_budget.label: Loss budget
loss_budget.tip: Common fixed-loss sizing input, not a guaranteed maximum loss. Actual package sizing amounts can differ because of caps and sizing policies.

sizing_loss_reference.label: Sizing loss reference
sizing_loss_reference.tip: An input used to size the trade, not its contractual maximum loss. Actual losses can exceed this amount; notional caps and sizing policies can also affect the final size.

bankroll.label: Bankroll (W)
bankroll.tip: Kelly notionals are λ·f*·W, where f* is each structure's full-Kelly size as a multiple of W.

fit_score.label: Fit to your view
fit_score.tip: How well the structure family matches the characteristics of your view (target distance, carry and so on), as a % of the maximum possible. It ranks types of structure, not specific strikes.

pnl_score.label: PnL score
pnl_score.tip: How a structure performs across a range of possible market outcomes, tuned to match an expert practitioner's process.

kelly_risk.label: Sizing exposure (Kelly)
kelly_risk.tip: Full-Kelly sizing-reference exposure (f* × sizing loss reference, before the λ haircut) as a share of W; not a maximum-loss bound. The notional column already applies λ.

premium.label: Premium
premium.tip: Net premium as a % of notional. Positive: you pay it. Negative: you receive it.

variant.label: Variant
variant.tip: How the strikes are chosen: by option delta (Δ), at-the-money forward, or by % premium.

strikes.label: Strikes
strikes.tip: Strike levels, in the order of the structure's legs.

notional.label: Notional
notional.tip: Size of the structure in base-currency units, set by the sizing method you chose.

audience_rules: Your reader is a quantitative PM who is new to FX-options structuring: comfortable with σ, vol, forwards and probability, but not with FX-options market shorthand or this tool's internal concepts.
Use the plain labels listed under TERMS by default. Mention the market term in brackets only when it helps, or when the PM uses it first.
Do not teach unprompted: no derivations and no pricing tutorials. If asked what a term means, answer in one to three plain sentences using its TERMS entry, then stop and offer to go deeper.
Keep rigour available, not in the way: lead with the decision-relevant point and offer detail on request.
Never lead with market shorthand (25d RR, fly, z-score, regime numbers) as the main label for a number.
